title: Light as field evidence
question: What can starlight honestly say about objects you will never visit?

intro.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Ridgeline to Dark Sky. The inherited log treats two bright white stars as twins because they look the same through the eyepiece.
I need that checked before the catalog treats a nickname as a fact. I'm on radio. Walk the basin. The light is the evidence.

afterTwins.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: The eyepiece twins were not the same light. There's a reddish star the old notes call an ember — like a coal.
See what its light actually shows. Don't let fire-color folklore write the catalog.

afterEmber.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Color folklore didn't survive the peak marks. Two more stars look about equally bright from the station.
Walk the west rim, then the east. The baseline is the distance. Appearance is not.

afterCairns.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Equal brightness, different shift. The unlabeled board at the station is empty on purpose.
Put the stars you actually measured on it. Don't copy a poster.

afterPlot.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: The board is starting to show a pattern. The wall cartoon still pretends every star lives one life.
Mass is not a vocabulary word here. Branch the two paths and check the remnant plate.

afterMass.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Not one life. Walk down to the Quiet Floor. There's a rock you can pick up.
I want to know what that stone has to do with the metal lines you can still measure.

afterFloor.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: The pan has ordinary stone and a quieter sky. The plate desk has galaxy plates whose lines don't sit at the lab rest.
Same element, moved pattern. Don't call a shifted line a red star.

afterShift.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: You've got expansion in the plates. Don't stamp a famous name on it yet.
Point the horn on the Quiet Floor. Assemble more than one line of evidence.

afterOrigin.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Three lines beat a slogan. The station poster still says a distant outburst is happening now.
Look later tonight at the nearby variable. Then tell me what the distant plate cannot claim.

afterLookback.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Looking farther can mean seeing earlier. There's an unlabeled envelope on the desk.
Say what the light shows. Say what you refuse. Then we'll make the case.

idle: The catalog stays honest only if the light does. I'm still on radio.
